name: simulacrum
lore:
# On the Transmutation of the Hollow Self: Simulacrum

To weave a *Simulacrum* is to engage in the ultimate flattery—and the ultimate deception. The casting begins with a biting, rime-crusted chill. As the magus channels the Weave through a slurry of snow and powdered ruby, the magic feels brittle, like sculpting shards of frozen time. It demands surgical precision; one slip of the will, and the mimicry shatters into slush.

Visually, it is a haunting transmutation. Snow swirls into a humanoid frame, translucent at first, until the ruby dust ignites, knitting flesh and fabric from frost. The resulting double possesses an unsettling, glassy stillness—a mirror with no soul behind the gaze.

Legend attributes this rite to the Arch-Magister Vaelin of the Wailing Peaks. Driven by the grief of his twin’s passing, Vaelin sought to replicate the man’s genius. He succeeded in form, but found only a silent echo. "I have built a palace of ice," his final journal entry reads, "and populated it with the ghosts of my own vanity."
